title: Degenerated current mirror
description: A source-degenerated current mirror: each leg puts a resistor in series with the source. Degeneration does two things. It raises the output resistance by the local-feedback factor $(1 + (g_m + g_{mb})*R_s)$ — the resistor sits in the source, so the source-body generator feeds back through it exactly as $g_m$ does — so the output current holds steadier against the output node voltage. And it improves matching: a threshold mismatch now competes with the IR drop across $R_s$, so its effect on the current divides by $(1 + (g_m + g_{mb})*R_s)$; the threshold generator sits at the gate, so only $g_m$ converts it to a current — but the source lift it causes feeds back through both source-referred generators, so the same $(g_m + g_{mb})$ factor divides it. The price is headroom, the resistor drops $I*R_s$ that the output node must clear on top of the device saturation voltage. Both legs are arranged to drop the same $I_{in}*R_s$ (the K-times output leg uses $R_s/K$), so the degeneration voltage matches and the source-body bias $V_{SB} = I_{in}*R_s$ is common to both. With both source nodes declared at that same potential and the gates on one wire, the output device binds the reference's own $V_{GS}$. Note that the arrangement is what the sheet declares rather than something the engine solves: it linearizes about $I_{out} = K*I_{in}$, so the degeneration feedback that would pull the output leg's source back toward that point is described by the matching rows, not by the systematic-error row. The demo table has no $V_{SB}$ axis, so that declaration only warns. The matching-improvement formula is exact only where threshold mismatch dominates; the LUT $g_{ds}$ and Pelgrom spread are the ground truth these rows annotate.

params.name: K
params.note: mirror ratio W_out/W_ref; degeneration mirrors are usually 1:1, and the output leg scales its resistor to R_s/K to keep the IR drops matched

params.name: R_s
params.note: reference-leg source-degeneration resistor; the output leg uses R_s/K

params.name: V_out
params.note: DC level of the node the mirror serves

doc.title: Reference (diode) device
doc.description: The diode-connected reference, its source lifted I_in*R_s above ground by the degeneration resistor. Its vds is the transistor's own diode drop; its source-body bias is the resistor drop. Exposes its width so the output side sizes as a unit-device multiple.

params.name: vsb_r
params.note: source above ground by the reference-leg IR drop (body grounded)

rows.name: sys_err
rows.note: lambda mismatch between the output transistor vds and the diode point

rows.name: R_s_out
rows.note: output-leg resistor; carries K*I_in and drops the same I_in*R_s as the reference leg

rows.name: V_deg
rows.note: the degeneration voltage dropped across each leg's resistor

rows.name: Rout
rows.note: output resistance boosted by local series feedback, with the resistor's own series contribution added back. Both source-referred generators feed back through R_s_out, so gmb belongs inside the factor; the trailing R_s_out adds about 1% at these defaults

rows.name: irel_out
rows.note: the OUTPUT device's own inversion level, read back from its operating point

rows.name: sigma_ratio
rows.note: degeneration divides the current spread by the local-feedback factor; estimate, exact only where threshold mismatch dominates

rules.note: the output node must clear the device saturation voltage plus the resistor drop (the headroom cost of degeneration)
